look_here_first: Look at the climbing organ first: trumpet creeper clings with short aerial rootlets, then confirm the large opposite odd-pinnate leaves with 7–11 sharply serrated leaflets.

project_inclusion.range_basis: USDA-derived county/native-status data document Bell, San Saba, Travis and Sutton as native target-zone counties. Hays is also present in the project Hays source list but is not needed for the threshold.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Widely planted and capable of escape; ornamental observations are not used to manufacture native counties.

best_field_traits: climbs by short aerial rootlets rather than tendrils
commonly 7–11 ovate to lanceolate sharply serrated leaflets
large orange to reddish-orange tubular/funnelform flowers in terminal clusters
four fertile didynamous stamens plus a staminode
long narrow 2-valved capsule with many flattened winged seeds
morphology_keys.comparison_training: The climbing organ is the fastest split from crossvine: rootlets in Campsis versus branched adhesive tendrils in Bignonia.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Crossvine has two leaflets plus an adhesive tendril. Coral honeysuckle has simple opposite leaves and berries. Catclaw vine has paired leaflets plus a claw-like tendril.
